title: Dates and clock time: 月, 号, 星期, 点
summary: Lets you say and ask the date, the day of the week and the time, as in 五月八号, 星期几 and 三点半.
structure: (Subject +) 星期 + 一 / 二 … 六 / 天
explanation:
Chinese dates and times are built from numbers plus a few time words. 月 is the month, 号 is the day of the month, 星期 is the week, and 点 is o'clock. So 五月八号 is "May 8th", 星期三 is "Wednesday" and 三点半 is "half past three".

Always go from big to small: month, then day, then weekday, then part of the day, then the clock time. For example: 五月八号，星期五，上午九点. To ask, put 几 ("which number") where the number goes: 几月几号？ 星期几？ 几点？ When you just state a date or time, you usually don't need 是: 今天星期五。 But to say "it's not", you need 不是: 今天不是星期五。

Weekdays are numbered from Monday: 星期一 is Monday, up to 星期六 (Saturday). Sunday is 星期天 or 星期日, never 星期七. For 2 o'clock, say 两点, not 二点. Minutes use 分 (八点十分 = 8:10), and 半 ("half") comes after 点: 七点半.

Time words come before the verb, not at the end like in English: 我八点上课 ("I have class at eight"). In speech, people say 号 for the day of the month; 日 is used mostly in writing.

examples.en: What time is it now? It's half past three.
I have class at nine tomorrow morning.

examples.zh: 他星期六晚上七点十分来我家。
examples.en: He's coming to my home at 7:10 on Saturday evening.

mistakes.why: There is no 星期七. Sunday is 星期天 (or 星期日).
For the hour "two o'clock", use 两, not 二: 两点.
In Chinese, the time comes before the verb, not at the end of the sentence.

why: 号 marks the day of the month, so 几月几号 asks for the date.
点 is for clock time (o'clock). It can't follow 几月几 to give a date.
分 means minutes, not a day of the month. Use 号 for the date.
几 asks for a small number, so 几点 is the normal way to ask the time.
多少 asks about larger amounts. It isn't used with 点 to ask the time.
什么 means "what thing". It isn't used to ask for a number, so 什么点 is wrong. Say 几点.

exercises.en: I get up at 7:30 in the morning.
why: 半 comes after 点: 七点半 means half past seven.
The order is wrong. 半 must come after 点, so it's 七点半, not 七半点.
个 is a measure word for counting things, not clock time. Use 点 for o'clock.
Correct. Sunday is 星期天, and you don't need 是 when you state a day.
There is no 星期七. Sunday is 星期天 (or 星期日).
星期六 is Saturday, not Sunday. Weekdays count from Monday (星期一), so Sunday is 星期天.
Correct. The time goes before the verb and runs from big to small: 下午 comes before 两点. It also uses 两 for 2 o'clock.
For 2 o'clock, use 两点, not 二点.
The time must come before the verb 上课, not after it.
Go from big to small: 下午 (afternoon) comes before 两点.

exercises.instruction: Turn it into a question asking which day of the week it is.
why: Correct. Put 几 in the number's place: 星期几.
几 replaces the number, and the number comes after 星期. So it's 星期几, not 几星期. (几星期 means "how many weeks".)
Weekdays are numbers, so ask with 几, not 什么.
几 replaces 五. You don't keep both the number and 几.
Correct. The positive sentence can drop 是, but the negative needs 不是.
不 can't go straight before a date. You need 不是 here.
不是 must come before the date, not at the end of the sentence: 今天不是五月八号.

exercises.en: I go to school at eight o'clock on Monday.
exercises.why: Time words go before the verb, from big to small (day, then hour), and they can come before or after the subject.
Dates go from big to small: month, then day, then weekday.
